resources.string: Temporarily suspends the app and stops its current process, blocking auto-start and background activity. It remains installed and can be restored at any time.
Disables the app more thoroughly. Its services and UI become unavailable and the launcher icon usually disappears. App data normally remains, but it cannot be used until restored.
Undo the frozen or disabled state and make the app available again.
Start the privileged helper first (long press needs shell privilege).
System apps and services cannot be frozen or disabled
No running apps or services.\nPull down to refresh.
Privileged helper is off — features are limited
Start the privileged helper for full functionality: exact CPU / memory data and the ability to end any app.

Full CPU/memory data and ending any app need the built-in helper, which runs with the same privilege as an adb shell — no root, no second app required.

• "Pair without a computer" opens the phone's Wireless debugging and posts a pairing notification. Tap "Pair device with pairing code", then enter the port and code from the notification shade.

• Or copy the command below and run it once from a computer.

The helper keeps running until the next reboot.
Command copied — paste it into a computer terminal with the device connected.
The helper did not start. Make sure Wireless debugging is on, then try again.
Enter the pairing port and 6-digit code from the notification shade
Open Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, then enter the port and 6-digit code here.
Port %1$s is set. Enter the 6-digit pairing code.
The pairing code is set. Enter the pairing port.
Port and code are ready. Starting pairing…
The pairing code is invalid or expired. Generate a new code and enter it again.
Could not connect to Wireless debugging
Pairing completed, but the connection is not ready. Make sure Wireless debugging is still on, then retry.
Pairing notification posted. Open the notification shade to enter the port and code.
Notification permission is required to enter the port and pairing code

Pairing is complete. Read the port after the colon under “IP address & port” in Wireless debugging, then enter it here. You can also turn Wireless debugging off and on so the app can receive it automatically.
Port %1$d did not connect. Open Wireless debugging and enter the port shown under “IP address & port”, or turn it off and on to refresh automatically.

Developer options are off.

1. Open Settings → About phone (on some brands it is under System).
2. Tap Build number seven times until Developer mode is enabled.
3. Go back to Settings → System → Developer options.

Return to this app and try wireless pairing again.

Wireless debugging is off.

1. Open Settings → System → Developer options.
2. Turn on Wireless debugging.
3. Return to this app and try wireless pairing again.

This device has no Wireless debugging entry in system Settings, so “Pair without a computer” cannot be used. Some manufacturers remove this feature even on Android 11 or later.

You can still start the privileged helper with a one-time ADB command from a computer:
1. Connect the phone by USB and allow USB debugging.
2. Copy the computer command and run it in a terminal.
3. Return to the app and tap “Check again”.
Wireless debugging screen not found; opened Developer options
No system settings screen is available on this device
Enter the pairing port shown in the Wireless debugging dialog
Enter the 6-digit code shown on screen
"%1$s" is a system app or service. Ending it may cause system instability, app crashes, data loss, or other unpredictable issues. Continue?
Requested to end %1$s. Without root the system may ignore it — use "App info" to force stop.
No system settings screen available on this device
You cannot end Activity Monitor itself
Detecting running apps needs the "Usage access" permission.\nTap here to grant it, then pull to refresh.
Full CPU/memory data and ending apps need the built-in helper.\nTap here for the one-time adb command, then pull to refresh.
